(Scch-9) Dated This The 02nd Day Of January 2024 Present: SRI.Shambhulingayya Mudimath.B.Com., Ll.B (Spl) Judge Scj, Acmm & Mact , Bengaluru. Mvc No.743, 744 & 745/2022 Petitioner in 1.Sri. C.Krishna Murthy, Mvc 743/2022: S/o.Late Chinmayi Krishna, Aged about 70 years, R/at No.456, Iii Cross, Iii Phase, Kalpavrikshanagar, Mysuru City - 570007 And also R/at: No.971/A, Iii Stage, Kesari, Kalpavriksahanagar, Mysore City - 570007. Petitioner in Kum.Mohitha.R., Mvc 744/2022: D/o.Raghavendra, Scch-9 2 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 Aged about 14 years, R/at No.455, Iii Stage, Kalpavrikshanagar, Kesare, Narasimharaja Mohalla, Mysore - 570007. The petitioner being a minor Rep. By her mother & Natural Guardian Smt.Lakshmi.K., D/o.Krishna Murthy.C., Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 1 Aged about 37 years.
texts.facts: All these petitions are arising out of the same accident, hence, these petitions are clubbed and taken together for common judgment. 3. The brief facts of all the petitions are as under:- SCCH-9 4 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 It is the contentions of petitioners that, on 18.10.2021 at about 6.45 p.m., the petitioner in MVC 743/2022 was riding his Honda Activa motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-55- U-8591 along with his grand daughters viz., S.Mohita (petitioner in MVC 744/2022) & Nethravathi (petitioner in MVC 745/2022) as a pillion riders for the purpose of visiting to Dasara Festival Lightings. When they reached A.P Road at Jayachamarajendra Circle, near Darga, at that time all of a sudden the driver of Swift Car bearing Reg.No.KA-11-N-1518 came in opposite direction, with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle and caused accident. Due to impact of said accident the petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. 4. Immediately after the accident the petitioner in MVC.No.743/2022 was shifted to Gopal Gowda Hospital, Mysore, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient. X-rays were taken, which revealed fracture injuries. After Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 3 SCCH-9 5 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 discharge from the hospital and as per the advice of the doctor, he has taken follow up treatment as an outpatient and till today he is taking treatment as an outpatient. Further contended that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 70 years and was doing business and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m., and was contributing his entire earnings to the family. Due to the accidental injuries he is suffering untold mental shock and pain. He cannot do his regular work. It is further contended that, he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicine, conveyance, food, nourishment and other incidental charges. 5. After the accident the petitioner in MVC.No.744/2021 was also shifted to Gopal Gowda Hospital, Mysore, wherein she has taken treatment as an inpatient. After discharge from the hospital and as per the advice of the doctor, she has taken follow up treatment as SCCH-9 6 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 an outpatient and till today she is taking treatment as an outpatient. Further contended that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 14 years and Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 4 was a student of VIII Standard. Due to the accidental injuries she lost her bright future, she is suffering untold mental shock and pain, unable to sit, squat, run, move and jump. It is further contended that, she has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicine, conveyance, food, nourishment and other incidental charges. 6. After the accident the petitioner in MVC.No.745/2021 was also shifted to Gopal Gowda Hospital, Mysore, wherein she has taken treatment as an inpatient. After discharge from the hospital and as per the advice of the doctor, she has taken follow up treatment as an outpatient and till today she is taking treatment as an outpatient. Further contended that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 11 years and was a student of V Standard. Due to the accidental injuries she lost her bright SCCH-9 7 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 future, she is suffering untold mental shock and pain, unable to sit, squat, run, move and jump. The petitioner further contended that, she has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicine, conveyance, food, nourishment and other incidental charges. 7. It is further contended that the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending Swift Car. Thus both the respondents are jointly Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 5 and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners for the injuries sustained by them. Hence, the petitioners prayed to allow these petitions and award compensation under all heads together with interest and costs. 8. In response to the court notices, in all the cases the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its written statement. The respondent No.2 remained absent and was placed exparte. SCCH-9 8 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 9. The brief contentions of the written statement of the respondent No.1 in all the petitions are as under: (a) This respondent contended that the petitions filed by the petitioners are not maintainable either in law or on facts. The petitions are bad for non joinder of necessary parties. It has denied the manner of occurrence of accident. It has contended that when three persons traveling on the alleged two wheeler thereby they have violated the seating capacity and violation of terms and conditions of the policy. The petitioners have violated the provisions of Motor vehicles Act by triple riding. The petitioner in MVC.No.743/2021 has lost the control over the alleged Honda Activa and fell down on the road. There was no negligence on the part of the driver of Swift Car, bearing Reg.No.KA-11-N-1518. It is further contended that Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 6 complaint was lodged after lapse of three days. The jurisdictional police colluding with the petitioners has lodged a false case against this respondent only in order to get higher compensation. SCCH-9 9 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 (b) This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy and it was valid as on the date of alleged accident and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy. The driver of the offending Car was not holding valid RC and DL on the date of alleged accident. Further this respondent has denied the contents of petition averments in toto and also denied the age, occupation and income of petitioners and medical expenses incurred by them and injuries sustained to them. With all these grounds, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.1. 10. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed : ISSUES IN MVC.No.743/2022 1. In order to prove their case, petitioner in MVC.No.743/2022 himself examined as PW1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to 8. In MVC No. 744/2022 & 745/2022 the natural guardian/mother of petitioners examined as PW2 & PW3 and got marked documents at Ex.P9 to Ex.P15 respectively. The Medical Record Technician was examined as PW4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.19. The respondent No.1/Insurance Company has examined its Asst. Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 & 2 and closed the side. The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- each in respect to the injuries sustained by them in RTA. It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 18.10.2021 at 6.45 pm the petitioner in MVC 743/2022 was riding the motor cycle along with two pillion riders who are the petitioners in other two petitions herein Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 9 and at that time the driver of Car drove his car in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of petitioners and caused the accident. Due to impact of said accident the petitioners have sustained injuries. The accident was caused sole negligence of Car driver and petitioners have sustained injuries. Hence these petitions for compensation. 15 . In order to prove the negligence the petitioner in MVC.No.743/2022 filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and examined as PW.1 and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition. This petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 14 sustained by the petitioner in the RTA.

Hence, I am of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.60,000/- . This petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the RTA. As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that accident was occurred due to the negligent on the part of offending SCCH-9 21 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 Car bearing No.KA-11-N-1518. As per Ex.P12/wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries: 1) Sutured wound over the left parieto occipital region for a length of 4 cm; 2) Laceration present over the left eye brow 2cmx1cmxbone deep; 3) Laceration present over the nose. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and also not produced any disability certificate to show that she is suffering from physical disability. Therefore, in view of non production of disability certificate and doctor evidence regarding disability, it cannot be considered as the petitioner is having physical disability due to the accidental injury. The Ex.P13/discharge summary of petitioner goes to Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 16 show that the petitioner was admitted on 18.10.2021 and discharged on 22.10.2021. It shows that the petitioner was admitted in the hospital as inpatient for a period of 5 days. However, the petitioner has not produced any disability SCCH-9 22 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 certificate to show that she is suffering from physical disability. The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P14 amounting to Rs.51,622/-. There is no dispute about medical bills. There is no physical disability to the petitioner to the accidental injury. Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained, treatment taken and medical bills produced by the petitioner, it is just and proper to award the Global Compensation. Hence, I am of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.1,30,000/- 22. Regarding Liability: The respondent No.2 though admitted issuance of policy in the name of respondent No.1 in his written statement but it has contended that the petitioner in MVC 743/2022 has violated the provisions of Motor Vehicle's Act by triple riding. It is further contended that violation of provisions of Motor Cycle Act is violation of terms and conditions of policy. The Respondent No.2 also SCCH-9 23 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 17 contended that the petitioners have contributed their negligence for occurring the accident. Admittedly, it is an undisputed fact that petitioners were riding in the motor cycle as on the date of alleged accident. The said fact has been admitted by PW1 in his cross-examination also. The petitioners contended that only on the part of negligence of offending Car driver the accident was occurred. The learned counsel for respondent argued that even if SCCH-9 24 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 minors were riding as pillion riders with triple riding that amounts to violation of Motor Vehicle Act and attract contributory negligence. In this regard he has relied upon the following reported judgments: 1) 2004 (1) KLJ 498 (P.S.Somaiah & anr V/s The Director, Bangalore Dairy and Others), wherein it Mohita R vs Oriental Insurance Co Ltd on 2 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16926790/ 18 is observed that - If any rider of Motor cycle violates Sec.128 of M.V.Act moving in a triple riding then contributory negligence to be considered and compensation should be apportioned on the apportionment of negligence. 2) 2003 (2) TAC 103 (Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Coimbatore Dvn) Ltd., Coimbatore V/s Abdul Salam & Others), wherein Hon'ble Madras High Court observed that riding the motor cycle more than seating capacity amounts to a negligence and contributory negligence be considered while awarding the compensation in accident case. 3) 2017 ACJ 418 (New India Assurance Co.., Ltd., V/s Hemanth & Others), wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that- in case of triple riding there is a contributory negligence and SCCH-9 25 MVC.No.743, 744 & 745/2022 liability to be fixed on apportionment to the insurance companies. 4) The unreported judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.5314/2009 (MV) between H.B. Hemakeshwarappa V/s Abdul Roop Khan The Hon'ble High Court observed that-in a motor cycle if three persons were riding it is a negligent on the part of rider of the motor cycle. Hence, not entitled for any compensation against the insurer.
